field_insights.observation: 9 independent paper measurements yield a numeric range of 20.7–24.5 km/s for Betelgeuse's radial velocity. Representative quoted values include '+21.91 ± 0.51 km/s' from an integrated photospheric spectrum, '24.5 km/s' from the core of Stokes I LSD profiles, and one record described as '24 to 17' indicating an observed variability range. One extracted sample '(-10.96, 0.69, 27.01)' corresponds to UVW space-velocity components relative to the Local Standard of Rest rather than a single radial velocity. Methods include Gaussian fitting of Stokes I LSD profiles, cross-correlation of spectral lines, photospheric neutral metal lines, and astrometric fits including a companion.
field_insights.interpretation: The measured radial velocity of Betelgeuse clusters around ~21–22 km/s, with excursions to ~24 km/s and quoted ranges as wide as 17–24 km/s. This scatter is physically expected for a pulsating red supergiant: Betelgeuse has a ~416-day fundamental radial pulsation mode and a longer ~2170-day secondary period, so photospheric velocity varies with pulsation phase, convection-cell motion, and episodic mass ejection. The '+21.91 ± 0.51 km/s' value likely represents a systemic or center-of-mass velocity, while '24.5 km/s' may reflect the instantaneous photospheric velocity at the epoch of observation. The '24 to 17' range explicitly captures temporal variability. The apparent inclusion of UVW components in the radial-velocity field is a parsing artifact: UVW are space-velocity components (including tangential motion), not the radial velocity. Cross-source differences therefore arise both from real stellar variability (pulsation, convection, possible low-mass companion orbital motion) and from methodological differences (LSR vs heliocentric vs center-of-mass reference frames, line-core vs integrated-profile measurements, different epochs).
cause_hypotheses: Pulsational velocity variations, especially the ~416-day fundamental mode and ~2170-day long secondary period
Large-scale convective motions and surface mass ejection altering line-profile centroids
Possible orbital motion induced by a low-mass companion, as proposed for Betelgeuse's long secondary period
Different velocity reference frames (LSR, barycentric, center-of-mass) and measurement methods (line core vs integrated spectrum)
Data extraction artifact: the UVW space-velocity vector being included as a radial-velocity value
field_insights.typical_range: ≈20.7–24.5 km/s for the compiled values; instantaneous photospheric RV may span ~17–24 km/s due to pulsation

suitable_use_cases: Studying radial velocity variability and pulsation of Betelgeuse, e.g., investigating the ~416-day fundamental mode and ~2170-day secondary period using multi-epoch measurements
Determining the systemic radial velocity from high-quality integrated photospheric measurements after applying pulsation-phase and reference-frame corrections
Cross-validating different measurement techniques (line-core fitting vs integrated profiles) for late-type supergiants
Serving as a teaching or methodological example of handling heterogeneous literature data for a well-known variable star
limitations: Only 9 independent measurements with heterogeneous methods and reference frames (LSR, heliocentric, systemic), limiting statistical robustness and comparability
One entry is a UVW space-velocity vector rather than a radial velocity; parsing artifacts may contaminate naive analyses
Intrinsic scatter from pulsation, convection, and episodic mass loss spans ~17–24 km/s, so a single epoch-independent radial velocity is not well defined
Coverage gaps: several source papers lack NIR photometry (h_mag, j_mag, ks_mag), restricting joint SED or extinction studies
Overall quality score is fair (0.585) with moderate calibrated confidence, so high-precision kinematic applications require careful filtering and re-assessment
recommended_caveats: Convert all velocities to a common reference frame (heliocentric/barycentric) and clearly distinguish systemic vs epoch-specific values before combining
Exclude or flag the UVW tuple entry; it is not a radial velocity and should not be used as such
If pulsation phase can be reconstructed from observation dates, use it to interpret instantaneous velocities; otherwise treat each measurement as a phase-dependent sample
Do not use these data for high-precision astrometric or dynamical calculations without re-evaluating uncertainties and removing outlier/parsing artifacts
For missing NIR magnitudes, consult original papers or external catalogs (e.g., 2MASS, Gaia, WISE) rather than assuming completeness of this dataset

overall_narrative: The data indicate that Betelgeuse’s measured radial velocity is broadly consistent with a baseline of approximately 21–22 km/s, punctuated by excursions up to ~24 km/s and a full quoted range of 17–24 km/s. This scatter is not anomalous but rather reflects the expected pulsational behavior of a red supergiant. The analysis covered a single field with no cross-field relationships, and the overall data quality was rated fair—suggesting that while the observed variability is physically plausible, the constraints are modest and primarily descriptive rather than providing new dynamical insight.
